claims.text: The X3's home screen shows a clock that ticks over every minute while the device is awake, and stops costing anything once it sleeps

honesty_conditions.text: Ticking happens only while awake on Home; no tick logic runs in SleepActivity or after deep sleep

claims.text: Clock rendering already exists and is reused, not rebuilt: the X3 board profile has a DS3231 RTC (freeink-sdk BoardConfig.h:959), halClock.isAvailable() is true on X3, and the Xteink theme draws a centered header clock on Home gated by SETTINGS.clockShowInHeader && halClock.isAvailable() (BaseTheme.cpp:374-376, XteinkTheme.h:39, HomeActivity.cpp:509, CoverGridHomeUi.cpp:145)

hard_questions.text: Is the existing device toggle (Settings > System > Clock > Show on home, default off) the switch, or should the xteink build default it on?
hard_questions.resolution: Firmware default: the xteink build ships Show on home (clockShowInHeader) ON

hard_questions.text: The RTC is only written by Clock > Sync now and the first Wi-Fi join (ClockSyncActivity.cpp:67, WifiSelectionActivity.cpp:533-537); the daily sync's SNTP sets system time only. Should the daily sync also write its SNTP answer to the RTC, so the clock stays correct without manual syncs?
hard_questions.resolution: Yes: when the daily sync's SNTP answer arrives, write it to the RTC

hard_questions.text: With no time zone picked, the clock shows UTC. Should the xteink build default the clock time zone to Asia/Jerusalem (matching the 06:00 rule), or keep UTC and set it on the device?
hard_questions.resolution: Default the clock time zone to Asia/Jerusalem behind the same xteink build flag

claims.text: HomeActivity::loop() (HomeActivity.cpp:303, no timer today) checks halClock.getTime() and calls requestUpdate() when the local minute differs from the last drawn minute, so both the classic and cover-grid Home layouts tick

honesty_conditions.text: A host or on-device check shows exactly one requestUpdate per minute change and none between changes (no redraw storm from the 50 ms idle loop)

hard_questions.text: With Time to sleep = Never (sleepTimeoutMinutes 31, getSleepTimeoutMs returns 0 at CrossPointSettings.cpp:364) Home would refresh 1440 times + 96 half refreshes a day on battery. Tick anyway, or only tick on USB power / when a sleep timeout is set?
hard_questions.resolution: Tick anyway when Time to sleep = Never; the user chose never on purpose

claims.text: The minute tick only runs when the clock is actually shown (clockShowInHeader on and halClock.isAvailable()), so a hidden clock costs no extra refreshes

honesty_conditions.text: With Show on home off or no RTC, Home issues zero timer-driven refreshes

claims.text: The tick must not keep the device awake: requestUpdate() never touches lastActivityTime (main.cpp:819-824), so auto-sleep at sleepTimeoutMinutes (main.cpp:897-901) still fires on schedule

honesty_conditions.text: With the tick running, auto-sleep fires at sleepTimeoutMinutes after the last button press, same as with the clock off

claims.text: No clock while sleeping: deep sleep is a full chip reset (main.cpp:171-177) and SleepActivity renders no time; the sleep image is unchanged
Reader screens are untouched: the reader's status-bar clock is the separate statusBarClock setting (SettingsList.h:501) and is out of scope

Each tick is a full-panel FAST_REFRESH (HomeActivity.cpp:482/559): Uc8253X3Driver does not override displayWindow, so PanelDriver.h:54 falls back to a whole-screen fast refresh, the same visual cost as a page turn

hard_questions.text: Accept a whole-screen fast refresh each minute with ghosting building until the next half refresh, or add a periodic HALF_REFRESH every N ticks (Home has no ghosting counter; the reader's pagesUntilFullRefresh at ReaderActivity.cpp:27 is the existing pattern)?
hard_questions.resolution: Home does a HALF_REFRESH every 15 minute-ticks to clear ghosting; the counter never blocks or delays auto-sleep

claims.text: The displayed minute may lag the RTC by up to 10 s because HalClock caches the RTC read for CLOCK_POLL_MS (HalClock.h:17, HalClock.cpp:41); acceptable for a minute clock
The X3 owner looking at the Home screen between books

honesty_conditions.text: The only person reading the X3 Home screen is its owner; no multi-user behavior is needed

claims.text: Today the Home header clock (Settings > System > Clock > Show on home, off by default per CrossPointSettings.h:264) shows the time of the last redraw and goes stale until a button press

honesty_conditions.text: Confirmed on the current X3 build: the header clock does not change without a button press

claims.text: Show on home (clockShowInHeader) defaults ON in the xteink firmware build
Home runs a HALF_REFRESH every 15 minute-ticks; ticking and the refresh counter never block or delay auto-sleep
The daily sync writes its SNTP time to the RTC so the clock stays correct without manual Sync now
Show on home defaults ON: CrossPointSettings.h:264 clockShowInHeader initializer becomes 1 for the xteink build

honesty_conditions.text: A freshly flashed/settings-wiped device shows the clock on Home without any user action

hard_questions.text: Your X3 already stores clockShowHeader=0, so a new default won't reach it. Add a one-time settings migration that turns it on for existing devices (it would also override anyone who deliberately turned it off), or will you flip the toggle once on the device?
hard_questions.resolution: No migration: the user flips Show on home once on the existing X3; the new default covers fresh/reset devices

claims.text: Home keeps a minute-tick counter and renders every 15th tick with HALF_REFRESH instead of FAST_REFRESH (HomeActivity.cpp:482/559); the counter lives in HomeActivity only and never touches lastActivityTime or preventAutoSleep, so sleep timing is unchanged

honesty_conditions.text: Over 30 awake minutes on Home, exactly 2 HALF_REFRESH renders occur (ticks 15 and 30); all other ticks are FAST_REFRESH

claims.text: When the daily routine's Wi-Fi join gets an SNTP answer (trustedtime::startSync in the routine port's joinWifi, callback onTimeSynced in lib/TrustedTime/TrustedTime.cpp:55-70), the routine writes the synced UTC time to the RTC from its own task before Wi-Fi turns off, never from the lwIP callback (which would race the render task's I2C RTC reads via HalClock)

honesty_conditions.text: The RTC write happens off the lwIP task and only after SNTP reports completed; with no internet the RTC is left untouched

hard_questions.text: Background SNTP (trustedtime::startSync) often hasn't answered when a quick LAN sync turns Wi-Fi off (SntpPolicy.h:13 notes tens of seconds on a hotspot), so the RTC write might rarely happen. Wait a bounded time (e.g. up to kClockSyncBudgetMs = 8 s, inside the 105 s routine cap) for SNTP at the end of the routine, or best effort only?
hard_questions.resolution: At the end of the daily routine, if SNTP has not answered yet, wait up to kClockSyncBudgetMs (8 s) inside the 105 s cap, then write the RTC; skip the wait when it already answered

claims.text: While the X3 sits awake on Home, the header shows the correct local time, changing within ~10 s of each minute boundary, with a ghost-clearing half refresh every 15 minutes, and it still auto-sleeps on its normal timeout

honesty_conditions.text: Verified on the X3 itself, not only in host tests

claims.text: HalClock's poll-and-cache (HalClock.cpp:37-54: _cachedUtc, _lastPollMs, _hasCachedTime, no lock) is guarded so the main-loop minute tick and the render task's formatTime can both call it without a torn 64-bit cache read or interleaved RTC I2C transactions

honesty_conditions.text: grep shows the routine never calls syncFromNTP/configTzTime/setenv(TZ) on the RTC-write path

honesty_conditions.text: A non-xteink env build (e.g. x4pro) still defaults clockShowInHeader to 0

scope_entries.finding: X3 has a DS3231 RTC at 0x68 (BoardConfig.h:959); localTime caches RTC reads 10 s; RTC written only by ClockSync and first Wi-Fi join
Home header already draws a centered clock when Show on home (clockShowInHeader, default 0) is on; nothing redraws it on a timer
loop() at :303 is input-only; render() repaints the full screen with FAST_REFRESH (:482 cover-grid, :559 classic); a minute-change check + requestUpdate() is the insertion point

auto-sleep keys off lastActivityTime, reset only by input or preventAutoSleep (:819-824, :897-901); self-requested redraws don't reset it; sleep is deep sleep/chip reset with no clock on the sleep image
X3 driver has no displayWindow override; PanelDriver.h:54 falls back to whole-screen Fast refresh, so no partial clock-only refresh on X3 without driver work
reader status-bar clock is a separate setting; reader is out of scope

routine's joinWifi starts background SNTP (trustedtime::startSync); onTimeSynced runs on the lwIP task; chooseLocalClock (DailyRoutine.cpp:265) prefers system/RTC so SNTP is not awaited; nothing writes SNTP time to the RTC except ClockSync and first Wi-Fi join
every persisted key is written (toJson loop :68) and a saved value overrides the initializer on load (:122), so changing the clockShowInHeader default does not flip the user's already-provisioned X3
shipped clock default is UTC (clockTimezone 255); the routine falls back to Asia/Jerusalem only for its 06:00 rule, so an unset device shows UTC on the Home clock
localTime mutates an unlocked cache; today only the render task (and the pre-activity routine) call it; the tick adds a second caller on the main task
